issues.description: The problem statement requires implementing config_system to accept a pointer to a Config struct, but the solution's config_system implementation treats the incoming stack value as a plain integer (comment: "logic expecting integer in [esp+4], not pointer") rather than a pointer to a struct. This mismatch will confuse students implementing config_system according to the specification: if they implement pointer-based logic (as requested), the solution/test expectations differ; if they follow the solution, they will violate the documented requirement. The template does not define config_system (intentional learning gap), but the divergent contract between problem text and solution is an unintentional structural inconsistency.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the required parameter contract consistent between problem statement and solution. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to state that config_system accepts an integer value on the stack (not a pointer), or (B) Modify the solution's config_system so it accepts a pointer to a Config struct and dereferences it appropriately. Example fix for option B (assembly sketch):

config_system:
    ; [esp+4] contains pointer to Config -> load pointer, then load field(s)
    mov edx, [esp+4]     ; edx = pointer to Config
    mov eax, [edx]       ; eax = first integer field of Config (adjust offset if needed)
    add eax, 10
    ret

Choose the fix that matches the intended teaching goal (pointer/struct handling vs. simple integer argument) and update the problem text or solution accordingly.
